clue.text: Force's colonel hosting first of military exercises

indicators.note: a host takes guests in, so the officer's short title holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: standard abbreviation for the army rank

indicators.note: the first of anything is where it starts, so only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: first of military
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: An army unit's colonel puts on a programme of military drills for his troops.
explanation.walkthrough: COL opens to take in M and PE: CO-MPE-L.
explanation.definitionFit: To compel someone is to oblige or coerce them, a straightforward verb synonym for making them do something.

clue.text: Keep this concert programme featuring tenor

indicators.note: a programme that features an item includes it within, so one letter goes inside

parts.note: a band's set is the list of pieces played at a gig
T is the abbreviation for tenor

explanation.surface: Someone advises hanging on to a concert programme that lists a tenor.
explanation.walkthrough: STET is Latin for 'let it stand', the proofreader's mark cancelling a deletion; 'Keep this' is what the mark tells the printer.
explanation.definitionFit: Proofreaders write the Latin instruction beside struck-out text meaning the original wording should remain as it was.

clue.text: Maize agriculture essentially fed Iowa in abundance

parts.note: maize is called corn in North America

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its heart, so only its central letter is used

parts.note: the sixth of eleven letters sits at the centre
a fed is an American federal agent, a kind of police officer
postal abbreviation for the US state

explanation.surface: Corn-growing feeds the economy of Iowa, a state of plentiful harvests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed' looks like a verb about feeding Iowa, but it is the noun for an FBI-type agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornucopia is the horn of plenty, and figuratively any overflowing supply or profusion of good things.

clue.text: Toy vehicles and craft around smaller map

indicators.note: turning around makes the word face the opposite way, so it is read backwards

parts.note: craft as skill or art
an inset is a small map set into the corner of a larger one

explanation.surface: A child's playroom holds model vehicles and craft materials spread around a little map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toy vehicles and craft' reads like one list of playthings; the definition stops at 'vehicles'.
explanation.definitionFit: A train set is a toy railway of engines, carriages and track, so it is a set of model vehicles.

clue.text: Formula 1 racetrack shortened, leading to car crash

indicators.note: something shortened has its end cut off, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: F for formula, with the digit 1 read as the letter I
Ascot is the famous English racecourse in Berkshire

explanation.surface: A shortened Grand Prix circuit leads to a crash on the track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'car crash' is meant figuratively, as in a car-crash interview; Ascot is a horse-racing course, not a motor-racing one.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a car crash is a humiliating disaster, and a fiasco is just such a complete, embarrassing failure.

clue.text: One spineless politician appearing at Women's Institute

parts.note: the WI is a British countrywomen's organisation
Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A weak-willed MP turns up to address a Women's Institute meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute is a British community organisation famous for jam-making and tough audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: A wimp is a feeble, timid person, someone lacking courage or backbone, matching the figurative sense.

clue.text: Bird from Maine, a nocturnal predator shrouded in dark

parts.note: postal abbreviation for the US state
taken as written

indicators.note: a shroud wraps round, so the predator sits inside the word for gloom

parts.note: taken as written
the owl hunts at night

explanation.surface: A bird from Maine is threatened by an owl hunting in the darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: The meadowlark is a North American songbird of grasslands, a specific example of a bird.

clue.text: Killer with chutzpah admitted to a crime

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: being admitted to a place means going inside it, so one word enters another

parts.note: a wrongdoing
cheeky nerve or impudence

explanation.surface: A brazen murderer confesses to a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: Chutzpah is Yiddish for cheek or audacity, and sass is the American word for the same back-talk.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a hired or political murderer, so a straightforward kind of killer.

clue.text: Best gold under the sun?

parts.note: to best someone is to outdo them
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether gold-medal sport is the best kind of thing under the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like an adjective but is the verb, and the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something outdoor happens in the open air, literally beneath the sky and its sunshine.

clue.text: Cold medicine's screwtop bottles

indicators.note: to bottle something is to hold it inside, so the letters lie within the words before

parts.note: running across the two words

explanation.surface: A cold remedy comes in bottles with screw-on lids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold medicine' reads as one phrase, but the definition is 'Cold' alone, a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Iciness is the state of being freezing, a noun for low temperature like cold itself.

clue.text: Proustian novel seemed pretentious

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into something fresh

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A long novel in the style of Proust struck readers as pretentious.
explanation.walkthrough: Proust's huge novel makes 'novel' look like a noun, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on airs is to behave affectedly superior, so in the past tense it matches having seemed pretentious.

clue.text: Platforms revolutionary charity work

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the following words are read backwards

parts.note: help given to those in need
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A radical charity's efforts are its platforms for change.
explanation.definitionFit: Podia is a plural of podium, the raised stand a speaker or winner stands upon.

clue.text: Reason to record diamonds being cut

indicators.note: cutting trims the end off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a log is a written record
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A jeweller has a reason to keep notes on diamonds being cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diamonds being cut' sounds like gem-cutting; it is a slang word losing its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is sound reasoning, the faculty of thinking things through, so it serves as the noun for reason.

clue.text: Private security devices cracked by veteran housebreaker

indicators.note: something cracked open has another thing forced in, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a GI is an American private soldier
veteran as an adjective, long-serving or old
fastenings for doors

explanation.surface: A seasoned burglar cracks private security locks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like an adjective for the security devices; it is a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: In the fairy tale the girl breaks into the three bears' home, eating their porridge and sleeping in their beds, so she is a housebreaker.

clue.text: Doctor Who's storyboard finally has climactic battles

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so just the closing letter is used

parts.note: the last letter of storyboard
to have is to own

explanation.surface: The storyboard for a Doctor Who episode ends with big final confrontations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Who' reads as the TV show's title, but 'Doctor' is the anagram signal working on 'Who's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A showdown is a final decisive confrontation, the climax of a dispute or Western film.

clue.text: Appreciate east Cornwall town's biscuits

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it
compass abbreviation
St Ives is a seaside town in Cornwall

explanation.surface: A visitor enjoys the biscuits sold in a town in east Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'east Cornwall' reads as one place, but 'east' is just E; St Ives is in fact in west Cornwall. Cornwall is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Digestives are a classic British wholemeal biscuit, often dunked in tea, so they are an example of biscuits.

clue.text: Develop rapport with posh young lady

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to get on well together, a verb
second meaning: the upper-class pronunciation of girl

explanation.surface: Someone tries to get friendly with an upper-class young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gel' imitates the plummy upper-class British way of saying girl.
explanation.definitionFit: People who gel come together and form a bond, while gel is also a jokey spelling for an aristocratic girl.

clue.text: Stray pouting over new muzzle

indicators.note: to stray is to wander off course, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: taken as written
abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A sulking stray dog is fitted with a new muzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Stray' a dog and 'muzzle' its mouth guard; here the muzzle is the open end of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunpoint is the tip of a firearm's barrel, the same part called the muzzle.

clue.text: Sympathetic detective evening the score

parts.note: a private investigator
tying a match makes the scores level

explanation.surface: A kindly detective helps a victim get even with a wrongdoer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evening the score' suggests revenge, but here it is drawing level in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitying means feeling or showing compassion for someone's suffering, close in sense to sympathetic.

clue.text: Extremely chic black suit

parts.note: fashionable, in vogue
spades is one of the two black suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A black suit is the height of stylishness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black suit' suggests clothing, but it is a suit of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'in spades' means to a great degree or in abundance, matching the adverb extremely.

clue.text: Deal with uncle trimming papa's beard

indicators.note: trimming cuts something away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker, so dealing with him is pawning
P is papa in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A relative trims his father's beard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker; the 'beard' is the botanical one on an ear of barley.
explanation.definitionFit: An awn is the bristly hair on grasses such as barley, collectively known as the beard of the grain.

clue.text: Drunk causes inn problems

indicators.note: someone drunk staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk makes trouble for the inn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like the person causing trouble, but it signals the letter shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuisances are annoying troubles or irritations, a near synonym for problems in everyday use.

clue.text: Prepare to fire half a dozen over the phone, showing bit of backbone

indicators.note: on a phone call you only hear words, so the spelling follows what is spoken

parts.note: you cock a gun's hammer before shooting
half of twelve

explanation.surface: Someone on the phone orders six people to get ready to shoot, displaying courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backbone' suggests bravery; here it is the spine, of which this is the bottom bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The coccyx, or tailbone, is the small triangular bone at the base of the spinal column.

clue.text: He abandons Muslim leaders for another religion's followers

indicators.note: whatever abandons a place leaves it, so those letters drop out

parts.note: sheikhs are Arab chiefs or Islamic leaders
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man leaves Islamic leadership to join a different faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the 'he' from SHEIKHS leaves S-IKHS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sikhs follow Sikhism, the faith founded by Guru Nanak, a religion distinct from Islam.

clue.text: Petty insult

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a snub or affront

explanation.walkthrough: 'Petty insult' reads as one phrase, but the adjective and the noun are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means small or trifling as an adjective, and as a noun it means a discourteous snub.

clue.text: Music producers reportedly have outstanding string players

indicators.note: a report is heard rather than seen, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: a debt still outstanding is one you owe
a bow is drawn across strings to play them

explanation.surface: Record producers reportedly have brilliant string musicians on their books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'string players' suggests violinists; it is the bows that play the strings.
explanation.definitionFit: Oboes are double-reed woodwind instruments, things that produce music, rather than record producers.

clue.text: Note how some call father Pop

parts.note: so, or soh, is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
da is a dialect word for father

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that some people call their father Pop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like another name for father, but it is the fizzy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda and pop are both names for a sweet carbonated soft drink.

clue.text: Bulk of opponent breaks chair while wrestling, making loud noise

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it
wrestling twists and throws things about, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the bulk is most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a competitor

explanation.surface: A hefty wrestler smashes a chair over a rival, causing uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: A charivari was a mock serenade of banged pots and pans; 'wrestling' looks like the scene, but it signals the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A charivari is a cacophonous din, originally the banging made to mock newlyweds, so a loud noise.

clue.text: Head of Interpol blowing cover identity, unfortunately

indicators.note: blowing a cover gives it away, so that letter is lost

parts.note: an assumed name

indicators.note: the head of something is its top, so only the opening letter counts

parts.note: the first letter of Interpol

explanation.surface: An Interpol chief sadly blows an undercover agent's false identity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing cover' sounds like exposing a spy, but 'blowing' just loses I from ALIAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of regret, used as an adverb meaning sadly or regrettably.

clue.text: Barely five hundred and fifty inhabiting North American island

parts.note: standard abbreviation

indicators.note: inhabitants live inside a place, so these numerals go within the word for an island

parts.note: a key is a low island, as in the Florida Keys
Roman numeral
Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Barely 550 people live on a North American island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely' looks like 'only just'; it means without clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Barely in the sense of without covering: nakedly means in an unclothed, bare way, an adverb.

clue.text: I clear view close to pine trees

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so just the last letter is used

parts.note: the last letter of pine
two trees, a yew and an ash

explanation.surface: Someone says they cleared a view by felling trees near a pine.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer speaks in the first person: an eyewash rinses the eye so it sees clearly. 'trees' supplies YEW and ASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is a lotion for bathing the eyes, so it could say it clears a person's sight, though it also means nonsense.
